author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Test anisotropic filtering without creating texture artifacts
summary: Use one oblique road or floor and a separate sprite-heavy scene to measure whether anisotropic filtering stabilizes distant detail, preserves texture-atlas borders, and remains correct across renderer APIs.
heroAlt: PCSX2 hardware-renderer OSD showing texture, draw, and frame statistics during a controlled filtering test

sourceLabels.pcsx2-performance: PCSX2 AF indicator and hardware-renderer counters

blocks.text: Choose a surface where viewing angle is the only problem

Anisotropic filtering is intended to improve texture sampling when a surface recedes sharply from the camera. A road, runway, tiled floor, or long wall is a better test than a front-facing sign. Establish that the title is already stable at native resolution and that mipmapping is not the unresolved fault. Record the active API, GPU driver, bilinear and trilinear behavior, mipmapping setting, internal resolution, and baseline frame-time evidence before enabling AF.

Do not treat the highest AF value as a universal upgrade. Some PS2 titles rely on unusual sampling or texture atlases, and forced filtering can pull color from a neighboring sprite, soften UI art, or expose seams.
Prepare one 3D route and one atlas check

items: A repeatable camera route over an oblique textured surface.
A separate menu or 2D scene with small fonts, sprites, or tightly packed artwork.
Automatic mipmapping and game-controlled filtering recorded as the baseline.
Post-processing, texture replacements, and sharpening disabled.
A clean per-game profile plus warm-session performance counters.

blocks.text: Raise AF while holding every other sampler value fixed

items: 1. Cold-boot the 3D route at native resolution and record texture stability from near to far distance.
2. Enable a moderate AF level while leaving mipmapping, bilinear, trilinear, renderer, and resolution unchanged.
3. Replay the route at the same camera speed and compare motion, not only the sharpest still frame.
4. Inspect the 2D scene for border bleeding, font halos, sprite seams, or altered pixel-art edges.
5. Increase AF one level only when the oblique surface still gains useful stable detail and the atlas check remains clean.
6. Close the session, switch to the other supported hardware API, and repeat the accepted level without changing the driver.
7. Return to the preferred API, move to the intended internal resolution, and repeat after the device is warm.
8. Store AF in this title's profile if another representative game fails the same value.

blocks.text: AF changes how samples are gathered along a surface whose projected footprint is stretched in one direction. It does not repair missing mip levels, invalid texture coordinates, or an upscaling alignment error. Testing a 3D route and a 2D atlas scene together protects against a result that looks sharper on roads only because it samples beyond artwork boundaries elsewhere.
Accept the lowest useful level that survives both geometry and atlas checks.

items: Oblique texture detail remains stable during camera movement.
Distant transitions do not sparkle or snap between visibly unrelated levels.
Fonts, sprites, health bars, and texture-atlas edges have no new bleed.
The chosen renderer produces the same intended sampling after a cold boot.
Warm frame time and thermal behavior stay within the recorded baseline budget.

blocks.text: Signs that AF is the wrong control

items: Front-facing and oblique surfaces flicker equally: investigate mipmapping or damaged textures.
Colored lines appear around sprites: restore game-controlled filtering for the title.
Only one upscale multiplier fails: isolate an upscaling alignment problem.
The image sharpens but motion becomes noisier: reject the higher level and compare the recorded route again.

blocks.text: Return sampling to the title's baseline

Restore anisotropic filtering to Off, Automatic, or the recorded default, close the emulation session, and cold-boot both reference scenes. Remove only the temporary AF override; preserve the mipmapping and renderer values that were never part of the experiment.
Display sharpening can conceal the result

A television, Android enhancement, or shader can exaggerate edges after the emulator frame. Disable those stages for evidence capture, then reintroduce them only after the direct output shows that AF itself is clean.
